name: session_create_request.v1
description: POST /v1/sessions request body (docs/13 §2.1): the one endpoint where context beats audio — the full ScreenContext IR and the last ~15 timeline events ride in the request body so the agent is context-complete before the peer connection exists. A Phase-3 client sends screen_context: null and recent_events: []; a Phase-4 capture-enabled client sends the real shapes. What this schema constrains is the ENVELOPE, and the server rejects only envelope failures with 400 VALIDATION_SCHEMA — a bad user_id, or recent_events that is not an array of {type, name, ts} objects. The screen_context payload itself is validated but NOT rejection-gated: an unsupported version, a schema-invalid IR, an unrecoverably oversized one, or a storage failure all still return 201, and degrade only the agent's context slot (docs/13 §2.1's 'a bad screen_context does not fail this call', docs/08 §7's 'the pipeline degrades context, never conversation'). Rejecting would mean a merchant on a stale app build cannot start a support call at the exact moment they need one; the earlier '400, whole body' wording in this description described an intent the implementation deliberately does not have. 'Never a partial ingest' does survive, and is about storage rather than status: a failing snapshot is discarded whole, never merged field-by-field, so garbage cannot reach the prompt. additionalProperties is false in the house input-schema style (protocol/tools/*.json): new request fields are a server-contract change (docs/13 §9), never a client improvisation.

user_id.description: Must equal the JWT sub claim — the server verifies and rejects a mismatch rather than honoring it; sub is the only principal in the system (docs/13 §1.2).

screen_context.description: Full screen_context/v1 IR — the last operational screen, support surfaces excluded (docs/07 §2.1) — or null when the client has no capture. A Phase-3 client always sends null. Shape authority is docs/07 and protocol/schemas/screen_context.v1.json; only the version marker is pinned here. An unknown version does NOT fail the request: SnapshotIngestor rejects the payload, nothing is written to ctx:{session_id}, and the response is the normal 201 — identical in every observable way to having sent null. (This field's description previously promised 400 VALIDATION_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION; that code exists and is raised, but for the docs/13 §6 signaling envelope, never here. See docs/13 §2.1 for why degrading beats rejecting on this endpoint.)

recent_events.description: The last ~15 app_event/v1 timeline entries, oldest first; may be empty (a Phase-3 client always sends []). Event shape authority is protocol/schemas/app_event.v1.json, which names this array as one of the three places it governs — clients send each variant's full field set (nav.from, tap.screen, input.value where non-sensitive, api_error.status + .code, dialog.visible), and the server stores what it is given. Only the {type, name, ts} canon every variant carries is pinned HERE, so this schema stays a shape check on the envelope rather than a second, drifting copy of that oneOf. Oldest-first is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the server RPUSHes this array into ctx:{session_id}:events in the order given and ContextCompressor.render_timeline_slot takes 'the newest 15' as events[-15:], so a newest-first array would hand the agent the oldest fifteen actions rendered backwards.
